confidence_level_percent.note: The write-up says '95% confidence'. It is stored here rather than rendered from delta by the guard, because a semantic transform in a guard is a computation in a guard.

fs_non_failing_groups.note: The count the FS AUROC rests on, and why the write-up calls it unstable.

loss_of_a_structurally_invalid_output.construction: evaluation.evaluate_document with a structural failure, through the frozen scorer. A pure function over no data: the always-answer contract scores a non-valid prediction as wrong.

mean_per_document_span_exact_f1.construction: 1 - unweighted mean group loss; the loss IS 1 - F1 per document
mean_per_document_span_exact_f1.note: A mean of per-document F1. NOT comparable to corpus-level micro Arg-C figures.

oracle_accepted_groups_total.construction: sum of accepted_groups across the trigger-count strata

zs_non_failing_groups.note: The count the ZS AUROC rests on. It and the FS count are why both are unstable.

interpretation: Ratios and counts the write-up quotes that were derived in prose from committed inputs and never stored. Each is recorded WITH pointers to the counts that produced it, so the pairing is auditable and scripts/check_paper_claims.py never has to divide - a guard that computes can be wrong in the same direction as the author. Nothing here selects a threshold or issues a certificate, and nothing here opens a split: it reads committed evidence JSON only.

content_bearing_share_of_group_loss.construction: 100 * channel group-level contribution / total group-level loss
content_bearing_share_of_group_loss.note: The GROUP-level share is 87.3%. The document-level share of the same channel is 86.2% and is a different quantity; the write-up quotes the group-level one.

parse_and_ground_rate_fs.note: 'Valid' is parseable AND grounded. It is NOT correctness: a span can point at real document text and still name the wrong entity or role.

parse_and_ground_rate_qa.note: 'Valid' is parseable AND grounded. It is NOT correctness: a span can point at real document text and still name the wrong entity or role.

parse_and_ground_rate_zs.note: 'Valid' is parseable AND grounded. It is NOT correctness: a span can point at real document text and still name the wrong entity or role.

ungrounded_span_separation.construction: zs ungrounded spans / qa ungrounded spans
ungrounded_span_separation.note: The write-up rounds this to ~16x. The unrounded value is 15.75.
